subject: Finlytics deployment pathing: Private endpoint sequencing & allowlist asks
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@finlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Finlytics deployment pathing: Private endpoint sequencing & allowlist asks

Hi Evan / Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick post-call recap and the concrete asks so your NetOps team has a single checklist to run against. Goal: confirm Private VPC path is feasible for PoC, and lock down the allowlist + basic security integration before we schedule a staging deploy.

Summary of what we discussed
- Customer priority: data residency + strict egress controls -> leaning Private VPC with PrivateLink (preferred) or VPC Peering fallback.
- Target PoC: 2-week functional window, canary traffic 10–20% then scale to full. Expected steady-state throughput ~800–1,200 rps for inference (peak bursts to 2k).
- Key operational asks: static egress IP range for allowlist, required inbound ports for PrivateLink, TLS cert process, KMS/HSM integration for model keys, and SOC2 evidence request.

Immediate action items for NetOps (please review and confirm):
1) Allowlist: we can provide a list of static egress IPs for PrivateLink endpoints (preferred). If you require VPC Peering, we need a CIDR exchange and routing table update.
2) Ports: outbound HTTPS (443) plus SSH (for ops tunnel, restricted), and ephemeral ports for health checks. See Ben's note (later in thread) for a short port matrix.
3) Proxy/NAT: confirm whether Finlytics will NAT outbound traffic at your egress or want us to egress from our managed NAT; impacts how we provide IP ranges.
4) PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink minimizes routing changes on your side but requires endpoint creation and interface ENIs; Peering allows lower latency but requires cross-account route entries and careful CIDR planning.
5) Certs & mTLS: If you require mTLS to our control plane, we support client certs via mutual TLS; otherwise TLS1.2+ with certificate pinning is standard.
6) KMS: our Private offering supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM); we need the IAM role and KMS key ARN for the PoC.

Attachments: I've uploaded a short netops questionnaire (Finlytics_NetOps_Questions.xlsx) and our Private VPC playbook (redwood_private_vpc_playbook_v2.pdf). Also adding a tentative PoC calendar invite (poC-schedule.ics).

Ask: can you loop in the NetOps distribution and confirm whether PrivateLink is acceptable, and whether Finlytics needs us to egress from a fixed set of IPs or you prefer to NAT on your side? If helpful, we can do a 30-minute NetOps-to-NetOps walk-through next week.

Thanks — Vivek

Thanks Vivek — useful recap. Priya and I reviewed the attachments briefly and routed the questionnaire to our NetOps alias. A couple of quick clarifications before we pull the NetOps folks in:

- Throughput: 800–1,200 rps looks reasonable for the PoC window, but our NetOps will want to see baseline connection counts and idle timeout assumptions. Can you share expected connection count per replica and whether Redwood supports connection pooling/keep-alive?
- Egress: Our preference is to NAT at our VPC egress (so we manage outbound IPs). That said, if Redwood can provide fixed IP ranges for its PrivateLink interfaces, that's acceptable — asking for both options so we can estimate firewall rules.
- Certs: We prefer mTLS for the control plane but will accept TLS for data plane; need an internal security review to finalize.

Looping NetOps (netops@finlytics.com) to confirm windows for a technical sync next week — prefer Tue/Wed morning PT. Evan

Subject: Re: Finlytics deployment pathing: Private endpoint sequencing & allowlist asks

Great — thanks Evan. Quick answers inline and a proposed agenda for the NetOps sync.

Connection counts / pooling
- Redwood inference uses HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive by default and supports HTTP/2 for some SDKs; typical connection count per replica for 1k rps workloads is ~600–800 concurrent connections (depends on token lengths & prompt patterns). We also offer connection reuse via our SDKs and an ingestion gateway option for long-lived TCP pooling (Marissa can add details).

Egress options
- Option A (preferred): Redwood hosts PrivateLink endpoints in your AWS account; traffic to our inference control plane will be via interface endpoints — we can supply a set of stable ENI IPs per region for allowlisting.
- Option B: VPC Peering — requires route table updates and cross-account peering connection (workable but more manual).

mTLS / certs
- We support client TLS cert ingestion for control-plane APIs (mTLS). For the data plane (tokenized inference traffic) we typically use mutual auth for Dedicated/Private deployments; for PoC we can enable client certs.

Proposed NetOps sync agenda (30m)
1) Quick intro & roles (5m)
2) PrivateLink architecture and endpoint creation steps (8m)
3) IP allowlist and egress model discussion (8m)
4) Port list & firewall rules (5m)
5) Next steps / ownership and SOW callouts (4m)

Marissa / Ben — want to add anything to the agenda? If Tue/Wed AM PT works for Finlytics we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Vivek
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finlytics deployment pathing: Private endpoint sequencing & allowlist asks

NetOps — quick port & IP sketch for your firewall team. Attaching the detailed sheet inside the questionnaire, but pasting the concise matrix here: 

Inbound (to Finlytics VPC)
- 443 TCP: outbound REST calls from Redwood -> Finlytics PrivateLink interface (required)
- 22 TCP: optional ops tunnel (bastion) — recommend limited source ranges and short windows

Outbound (from Finlytics VPC to Redwood)
- 443 TCP: inference requests (HTTPS)
- Ephemeral TCP: 49152–65535 (health checks & ephemeral client ports)

Egress IP options
- If Finlytics prefers to NAT outbound: provide us with the NAT IP(s) and we will whitelist on our side (no infrastructure change required on your routers).
- If using PrivateLink hosted endpoints: we will produce a deterministic list of ENI IPs (per AZ) for you to allowlist; expect ~4–6 IPs per region depending on HA topology.

Timeouts & health checks
- Idle timeout: 60s recommended for PoC, adjustable for production.
- Health check: TCP/443 with a 5s interval / 3 failures to mark unhealthy.

Note on performance: to support the ~2k burst capacity we recommend at least 3 replicas in the PoC cluster behind our routing; we can provision autoscaling behavior during the PoC but need confirmation on allowed burst concurrency.

I'll include a condensed CSV in the questionnaire for your firewall team.

-ben

- We'll try NAT-at-our-egress first (so Finlytics manages outbound IPs) — we'll provide the NAT pool by Monday.
- We'll run a CIDR check and confirm whether PrivateLink vs Peering is preferable after the tech sync. Tentatively leaning PrivateLink for simplicity.
- Security team wants mTLS on the control plane; we’ll bring that up on the call.

Please send calendar invite and NetOps call link. Also, could Redwood share an example KMS role ARN pattern we should prep for?

Thanks — Evan
